title.narrative: Emergency rehabilitation of agricultural productive assets of farmers affected by the 7 October 2023 crisis in the Gaza Strip

description.narrative: ltpgtThe ongoing conflict in the Gaza Strip resulted in significant damage to the agricultural sector, including cropland, greenhouse, agricultural infrastructure and agricultural wells. ltbrgtTo respond to the huge resulting needs, the proposed intervention will follow an area-based approach to support a total of 228 households (HHs) (1,368 individuals) and rehabilitate 82.000 m2 of agricultural land across all the governorates of the Gaza strip.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtActed will first conduct preliminary assessments of Housing, Land and Property (HLP) and Explosive Remnants of War (ERW) to identify the lands that will be targeted for rehabilitation, in respect of the community’s safety and property rights. Following the land’s identification, Acted and its local partner Gaza Urban Peri-urban Agriculture Platform (GUPAP) will select 171 cash-for-work beneficiaries (BNFs) for the rehabilitation of open lands (OL) and greenhouses (GH) (82 dunums in total, 82.000 m2), which will be cultivated by 57 targeted farmers. Rehabilitation includes emergency repairs on the water networks benefiting the selected OL and GH, contributing to addressing gaps in the water supply across the targeted areas.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtActed and GUPAP will support the 57 targeted farmers, prioritizing female farmers, to restore their agricultural productive capacity, building upon the local knowledge and expertise. The selected 57 farmers will benefit from conditional cash grants to purchase goods such as seeds, seedlings and fertilizer to cultivate the selected OL and GH.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtBy restoring agricultural productive assets of the farmers and ensuring better access to water resources and the cultivability of their land, farmers will be able to resume their farming activities and enhance their livelihood and resilience. Beyond the direct impact on vulnerable farmers, increased agricultural production will increase food availability and affordability throughout the target areas. In fact, the intervention will aim to rehabilitate land, in order to resume agricultural activities, including reactivation of vegetable and fruit production to improve diet diversity and reducing food gaps in Gaza, which had been particularly affected by the 15-month conflict. A gender-sensitive and integrated protection approach will be implemented, prioritizing female farmers, female-headed HHs, Persons with Disability (PwD), the elderly, and unaccompanied children, in compliance with the standard selection criteria shared by the FSS Cluster.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe intervention will be embedded into Acted’s ceasefire response strategy, which aims to switch the focus from a specific site and sector perspective to a broader, area-based and multisectoral one. Since all areas of Gaza have been severely affected by the conflict and infrastructure damage, the entire population is considered as in need of assistance. To ensure an effective response, activities will be coordinated with local communities who are represented by Community Relief Fora (CRF) within identified neighborhoods and sub-areas (Murabas –or blocks– and Haras). This approach will help identify the most urgent needs of the farmers at the area-level to improve the humanitarian response by ensuring better coordination with the community and service providers through efficient two-ways communication. ltbgtActed will closely coordinate with the FSS Cluster, its members and the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) throughout the entire project implementation to ensure the de-duplication of the BNFs and to avoid any omission of services.lt/bgtlt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtActed’s MEAL team will ensure strong monitoring and accountability mechanisms throughout implementation. On-site and post-distribution monitoring (PDM) will be conducted to assess impact, identify gaps, and adapt interventions as needed. Acted Feedback mechanism (AFM) will be in place to ensure inclusiveness and responsiveness to BNFs’ needs, reinforcing Acted’s commitment to a principled, needs-based, and people-centered humanitarian response.ltbrgtlt/pgt
